trust_decision.summary: OcspClient.validateResponse decides whether a fetched OCSP BasicOCSPResp is accepted for the queried certificate; at the pinned commit it checks response count, optional nonce and signature but never that the SingleResp CertID (issuer hashes + serial) matches the certificate queried, so any validly signed response from the same issuer/responder (e.g. for another cert) is accepted; OcspServerCertificateValidator then trusts getResponses()[0].

landing_point.why: validateResponse is the only place the OCSP response is checked (count/nonce/signature); 'missing CertificateID validation' leads straight here.

fix_sites.entry_point: public OcspServerCertificateValidator (pipeline handler) -> SslHandshakeCompletionEvent -> package-private OcspClient.query -> validateResponse (CertID issuer+serial match added, fix.diff:2609-2615)
same; unchecked (BasicOCSPResp) cast replaced by instanceof check for non-basic / null responseBytes (fix.diff:2547-2564)

public OcspServerCertificateValidator.userEventTriggered: handshake event now held until OCSP result, reads paused, out-of-date response returns instead of continuing, null nextUpdate handled (fix.diff:2795-2960)
internal HTTP handler installed by OcspClient.Initializer; adds response timeout, channelInactive failure, release (fix.diff:2669-2741)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the validator ordering/fail-open part: 'the advisory is about CertID matching in the OCSP response, the event-ordering and stale-date handling in OcspServerCertificateValidator is pre-existing design (closeAndThrowIfNotValid=false lets the app decide)'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Delegated-responder responses (signed by an included responder cert chaining to the issuer) and responses without nonce when validateNonce=false must still be accepted; with closeAndThrowIfNotValid=false the validator must forward OcspValidationEvent instead of closing; the fix also accepts a null nextUpdate (RFC 6960 optional).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a netty-provided default stapled-response verifier (concrete OcspClientHandler subclass) that parses engine.getOcspResponse(), checks signature and status but not CertID
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: OcspClientHandler is abstract and pushes verification to users; a convenience implementation reusing OcspClient.validateSignature is a natural maintainer addition, and it sits in a different code path (stapling, OpenSSL engine) from the query route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-issuer OCSP response cache consulted before querying, returning a cached BasicOCSPResp without re-matching CertID to the current certificate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: OCSP caching is a common optimisation; the cache key would plausibly be the responder URL/issuer, and the CertID check in validateResponse would not run on a cache hit (cache boundary lesson).
